review_candidates.description: Since 2004, OSIbeyond has delivered managed technology and cybersecurity services on a founding principle: outstanding technical expertise, matched by an exceptional customer experience. Today, that commitment is delivered through OSIbeyond ONE, our integrated technology platform that unifies IT operations, cybersecurity, Microsoft 365, cloud, automation, AI, and expert support into a single, continuously managed environment. The platform is built on a clear operating philosophy: Automation First. AI Enabled. People Powered. Within that model, the overwhelming majority of routine service requests are resolved by automation, with the Level 2 (Human Support) team confirming AI-extracted parameters and initiating workflows. What remains is, by definition, the hard part: the intermittent fault that spans identity, network, and application layers; the migration that touches every user in an organization; the server, firewall, or hybrid cloud dependency that no runbook anticipated. The Level 3 Engineer is where that work lands, and where it gets solved. This is the senior engineering seat in Technical Services. The Level 3 Engineer is the escalation authority for the Level 2 team, the engineer who scopes, leads, and delivers client infrastructure projects, the steward of OSIbeyond’s own internal infrastructure, and a working partner to the Automation Engineering team in deciding what gets automated next. Every escalation resolved here is also studied here: the engineer is expected to ask whether a class of problem should ever reach a human again, and to help design the workflow, detection, or self-healing logic that ensures it does not. The position spans a range of seniority. Engineers at the earlier end of that range concentrate on resolving the most complex escalations and executing pre-scoped project work to a high standard. Engineers at the senior end own project scoping and delivery, direct the work of peers on complex migrations, design architecture, and carry a larger share of automation design and technical leadership. Compensation and scope of ownership grow with demonstrated expertise and impact within the position. This position is suited to a technically accomplished engineer who has outgrown ticket volume and wants ownership of the difficult, consequential work: complex escalations, infrastructure and project delivery, and the engineering of automation that lifts an entire team. The successful candidate combines deep Microsoft 365, Azure, Windows Server, and network expertise with sound judgment under pressure, disciplined documentation, and the professionalism to represent OSIbeyond in front of client leadership during a high-stakes incident or a major project cutover. The engineer owns the escalation queue end to end. Each escalation is triaged for business impact, diagnosed to root cause rather than symptom, resolved within service level commitments, and documented so that the resolution becomes reusable knowledge, an updated procedure, or a specification for new automation. Where an automated workflow has failed or produced an unexpected result, the Level 3 Engineer is the engineer who determines why, corrects the environment, and works with Automation Engineering to harden the workflow. On the project side, the Director of Engineering leads discovery and scoping, and the engineer takes the work from there through delivery: solution design, detailed implementation plans, cutover execution, post-project validation, and client-facing training on what was delivered. Projects range from server, network, and identity deployments to tenant and data migrations and cloud modernization. The engineer prepares the detailed directions that allow peers to execute project tasks reliably, and manages scope, schedule, and client communication throughout. Across all of this work the engineer uses OSIbeyond-approved AI assistants to accelerate diagnostics, scripting, planning, and documentation, and holds every AI-assisted output to the same standard of verification as any other engineering work. The Level 3 Engineer also raises the technical ceiling of the team through mentorship, peer review, and the on-call rotation. The short version You'll be a senior generalist across desktops, servers, networks, firewalls, cloud, and cabling - not a password-reset seat. Our mission: keep organizations running, their teams supported, and the people they serve taken care of - using technology that solves today's problems, anticipates tomorrow's, and handles the ones no one saw coming. We're small enough that your work is visible and your name is on it. There's no layer of management between you and the decision. What the job actually looks like -- A Tuesday might be: remote-fixing a mail flow issue in Microsoft 365 before 9 a.m., driving to a client in Fishers to swap a failed switch and clean up a rack that's been a mess since 2019, taking a call from a controller who can't get QuickBooks to talk to the network share, then closing out with documentation so the next person isn't starting from zero. Client support & troubleshooting Handle client requests by phone, remote session, and onsite visit Diagnose and resolve issues across workstations, printers, firewalls, networking, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, QuickBooks, email, cameras, and IoT/sensor devices Communicate clearly with non-technical clients and keep them informed while you work Document your work accurately in the PSA/ticketing system - steps taken, root cause, resolution Pull in other Tech365 team members when a second set of hands or another specialty is the faster path Network & infrastructure Install, configure, and maintain firewalls, routers, switches, modems, and access points (UniFi, SonicWall, and similar) Run, terminate, and test structured cabling; troubleshoot existing wiring Leave every rack organized, labeled, and better than you found it Systems & cloud administration Support virtualized environments on Hyper-V and similar platforms Administer Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Google Workspace, and other SaaS platforms Maintain backup systems, verify restores, and support RMM and remote management tooling Hardware & field work Hardware setup, replacement, and troubleshooting with minimal supervision Work on servers, racks, and infrastructure at client sites to keep uptime where it belongs Lift up to 60 lbs, climb ladders, and work in office, retail, and industrial environments What success looks like First 30 days - You're closing tickets independently across our top client environments, and your documentation is good enough that someone else could pick up your work cold. First 90 days - You're the primary tech on a defined set of clients. They ask for you by name. You've caught at least one problem before the client noticed it. First 6 months - You're running project work start to finish: a firewall replacement, an office move, a server migration. You've improved at least one thing about how we do the work, because you got tired of doing it the slow way. What we're looking for Required 3+ years in IT support or a similar technical role - MSP experience strongly preferred Solid troubleshooting across Windows, networking (IP/DNS/DHCP/VLANs), and business applications Hands-on with Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace administration Experience with firewalls, backups, and remote tooling (RMM, PSA, ticketing) Comfortable working a ticket you were handed with incomplete information - you ask good questions, then move Strong client communication; you can explain a problem calmly to someone having a bad day Valid driver's license and reliable transportation You can pass a background check (many of our clients require it) Helps you stand out UniFi and/or SonicWall configuration depth Hyper-V or VMware administration Structured cabling experience - you've terminated more than a handful of drops Exposure to HIPAA-aware or PCI-aware environments CompTIA A+, Network+, or Microsoft 365 Fundamentals - useful, but your track record matters more than the paper The honest part -- We'd rather tell you now than waste your time in round three. Some situations you'll walk into with almost nothing — a client who says "the internet is broken" and nothing else. Figuring that out is the job, not an inconvenience of the job. There is an on-call rotation. Roughly one week in rotation. Our clients don't only break between 8 and 5. This is a field role. You'll drive across Marion and Hamilton County most weeks. Mileage is reimbursed at the federal rate. It's physical some days. Ladders, cable pulls, 60 lb boxes, dusty server closets, occasionally a manufacturing floor. You're the face of Tech365 on-site. How you present matters as much as whether the fix works. Where you land isn't decided by your resume or how well you interview - it's decided by what you actually do during the paid working interview. Technician II - $48,000–$56,000 You close tickets independently across Windows, Microsoft 365, and Google Workspace. You handle hardware and standard client requests without supervision. On infrastructure work — firewall changes, switch configuration, virtualization — you're capable but you still check in. Senior Technician - $58,000–$68,000 You walk into an undocumented client network and have it mapped and stabilized the same day. You configure UniFi and SonicWall gear without a runbook. You own projects end to end and your documentation is good enough that nobody has to ask you a follow-up question. Lead Technician - $68,000–$75,000 Everything above, plus you set the standard. You're the escalation point other techs route to, you catch problems before clients report them, and you improve how the whole team works. If you come in at Technician II and perform at Senior, we move you at the 90-day review. That's a commitment, not a maybe. How we hire Phone screen (~20 min) - role fit, independence, on-call, logistics Technical conversation - real scenarios, not trivia Paid, on-site working interview - you spend a day with us and with real clients That third step is deliberate. Most MSPs hire off a video call and hope. We'd rather both of us know exactly what we're signing up for. You get paid for the day either way. How we work Integrity First - We do what we say. Honesty and transparency in every interaction. Own the Outcome - No finger-pointing. We take responsibility and solve the problem. Team Before Self - We back each other up and share what we know. Client Obsessed - Our clients' success is our success. We go the extra mile every time. Continuous Improvement - Never settle. Always find a better way. Families Matter - Our decisions affect the families of teammates, clients, and partners. We act with care, respect, and responsibility. If those read as things you already do without being asked, apply. Benefits: Health insurance Paid time off Professional development assistance
